summary: This note is a long Wikipedia-style overview of FC Barcelona, covering the club's rivalry with Real Madrid (El Clásico), its finances and valuations, and its history from founding in 1899 through the Cruyff, Guardiola and Messi eras. It lists the club's major trophies and records, including multiple trebles, sextuple success, and the club's youth academy La Masia and supporter culture. It also notes a 2014 FIFA transfer ban and the club's record goalscorers.
one_line: Overview of FC Barcelona's history, rivalry with Real Madrid, finances, trophies, records and key players and managers.
key_facts: FC Barcelona was founded in 1899 by a group of Swiss, English and Catalan footballers led by Joan Gamper.
The 2009 season saw Barcelona become the first Spanish club to win the continental treble of La Liga, Copa del Rey and the UEFA Champions League.
In 2009 Barcelona became the first football club to complete the sextuple, winning six out of six competitions in a single year.
In June 2015 Barcelona became the first European club in history to achieve the continental treble twice.
Barcelona scored 180 goals in 2015 in all competitions, setting the record for most goals in a calendar year and breaking Real Madrid's record of 178 goals scored in 2014.
Lionel Messi is Barcelona's record league scorer with 305 goals in La Liga.
In April 2014 FIFA banned the club from buying players for two consecutive transfer periods, together with a fine of CHF 450,000.
In 2010 Forbes evaluated Barcelona's worth at around €752 million (USD $1 billion), ranking them fourth behind Manchester United, Real Madrid and Arsenal.
Johan Cruyff was bought for a world record £920,000 from Ajax in the 1973–74 season.
Diego Maradona was signed for a world record fee of £5 million from Boca Juniors in June 1982.
The club's motto is "Més que un club" (More than a club), reflecting its symbolic role in Catalan culture and Catalanism.
As of December 2015, Barcelona had won 23 La Liga titles, 27 Copa del Rey titles and five UEFA Champions League titles.
Barcelona's Camp Nou was built between 1954 and 1957, with construction ending on 24 September 1957 at a final cost of 288 million pesetas, 336% over budget.
Pep Guardiola said of Cruyff's legacy, "Cruyff built the cathedral, our job is to maintain and renovate it."
The 2014–15 season saw the MSN trio of Messi, Suárez and Neymar score 122 goals in all competitions, the most in a season for an attacking trio in Spanish football history.

entities.role: founder of the club who became club president in 1908 and spent 25 years at the helm in total

entities.name: Johan Cruyff
entities.role: player and later manager who led Barcelona to four consecutive La Liga titles from 1991 to 1994

entities.name: Pep Guardiola
entities.role: former Barcelona coach and early La Masia graduate who won 14 trophies in four years

entities.name: Diego Maradona
entities.role: player signed from Boca Juniors for a world record £5 million in June 1982

entities.name: Terry Venables
entities.role: manager hired in 1984–85 who won La Liga with the club

entities.name: Ronald Koeman
entities.role: Dutch international whose free kick goal beat Sampdoria in the 1992 European Cup final

entities.name: László Kubala
entities.role: player signed in June 1950 who later scored 196 goals in 256 matches

entities.name: Tito Vilanova
entities.role: assistant manager who took over from Pep Guardiola and resigned in July 2013 due to returning throat cancer

entities.name: Samuel Eto'o
entities.role: leading scorer in the 2006–07 season who publicly criticized coach Frank Rijkaard and Ronaldinho
